newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola futures close higher, grains lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola futures close higher, grains lower.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher supported by crusher buying and higher CBOT soybean futures, traders said.
Flaxseed futures closed lower pressured by light hedge selling and feed grains ended lower.
In canola, slight improvement in processor margins sparked crusher buying but poor export demand and a strong Canadian dollar had some traders doubting prices will move higher.
Canola closed up C$0.10 to C$2.50 with May up C$2.20 at C$425.20 per tonne and July up C$0.10 at C$429.60.
Flaxseed futures were lower pressured by hedge selling, the result of increased farmer selling this past week. Flaxseed closed down C$2.00 to C$2.10 with July off C$2.00 at C$339.20.
Market talk of increased flaxseed acreage this year prompted selling in the new-crop November, which closed down C$2.10 at C$320.00.

Feed grain futures were lightly traded with wheat and barley pressured by light commercial long liquidation. Wheat closed down C$1.20 to C$0.10 with July off C$0.90 at C$167.60. Barley was off C$0.70 to C$0.10 with July off the least at C$141.00.
Oats and feed peas were lightly traded. October oats closed down C$1.00 at C$120.00. Feed peas close down C$0.50 to C$1.50 with July unchanged at C$201.00.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
